clue.text: Subject of monarch protected by it — plan to be devised

indicators.note: the royal word sits inside the shuffled letters, as if guarded by them
letters that are yet to be devised are worked into a new order

parts.note: a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A ruler's subject is shielded while a scheme is still being drawn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be devised' makes TALPOINT, which 'protected by' wraps round the royal word. 'Subject' looks like a monarch's subject but means a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking point is a topic for discussion, the subject of a conversation.

clue.text: Religious head is certain to be under a hundred

indicators.note: in a down clue the second word is placed below the first

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone devout is certain they will stay below a hundred years old.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk or priest, a head marked out for religious life.

clue.text: Leaf from white notebook

parts.note: lily-white: the lily is a byword for whiteness
a pad is a notebook of tear-off sheets

explanation.surface: A page torn from a white notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaf' looks like a page from the notebook, but it is the floating leaf of a water plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily pad is the broad floating leaf of a water lily.

clue.text: Communicates between turns

definitions.meaning: talks or deals with one another
read as INTER (between) plus ACTS (turns, as on a variety bill)

explanation.surface: Someone talks in the gaps between their spells of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to communicate with others, and split as inter-acts it means among the acts, or turns, of a show.

clue.text: Mean to cause annoyance

definitions.meaning: as in 'what are you driving at?', to intend or imply

explanation.surface: To be nasty in order to irritate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to imply something and to keep needling someone.

clue.text: Subdue urge to support work

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word goes beneath the other

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to press is to urge

explanation.surface: Advice to crush a strong impulse by backing your labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to keep down or crush by harsh rule, to subdue.

clue.text: Is a coin working capital?

indicators.note: the letters are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether a working coin counts as money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges IS A COIN. 'capital' looks like money but is a city: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Representation from angry works unit

parts.note: cross means angry
a section is a department or unit in a works or factory

explanation.surface: A depiction of an irate factory department.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-section is a typical sample representing the whole, or a drawing of a cut-through view.

clue.text: Permit put on phone lock

indicators.note: in an across clue the word put on comes after the other

parts.note: to ring is to phone
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: Being allowed to fit a lock to your telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is a lock of hair, not a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a curled lock of hair.

clue.text: Hot and humid, runs out of immediate interest

indicators.note: the runs letter is taken out, leaving the weather word without it

parts.note: tropical weather is hot and humid
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A muggy climate that drains away whatever is pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical is relevant to current affairs, of interest right now.

clue.text: Miss strong (the poet) might get angry

parts.note: to lose is to miss, as in miss an opportunity
Patience Strong was a popular English writer of sentimental verse, so 'Miss Strong' is Patience

explanation.surface: A lady poet called Miss Strong might lose her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Strong' reads as one poet, Patience Strong, a British writer of homely verse, but 'Miss' gives LOSE and 'Strong (the poet)' gives her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose patience is to stop tolerating something and become angry.

clue.text: How to ruin cold dinner outside

indicators.note: the meal sits outside, wrapping round the cold letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal, dinner
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A recipe for spoiling a meal by serving it chilled out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck or sink it.

clue.text: Tensions don't open locks

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: stresses are tensions

explanation.surface: Strains that fail to unfasten the locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' are locks of hair, not door locks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresses are long locks of hair.

clue.text: Zip back on the river as an afterthought

indicators.note: the whole assembly is turned to run the other way
the postscript is tacked on after the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales and England
PS, postscript, is added as an afterthought

explanation.surface: Someone zips back up the river as a late addition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole of DEEPS round; 'Zip' looks like part of the action but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is energy and pace, speed.

clue.text: Pack musical instrument for dodgy dealer

parts.note: a pack is a set of playing cards
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Bundling up a harp to give to a shady trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a cheat at card games, one who deals crookedly.

clue.text: First principles in game obscure — sent off!

parts.note: RU is rugby union
to dim is to obscure

indicators.note: off signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A rugby player is sent off for some obscure breach of the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SENT into ENTS. 'sent off' looks like a referee's decision but only marks the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudiments are the basic elements of a subject, the first things learned.

clue.text: Concentrated on studies in church duties, primarily

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written
dens are studies, private work rooms

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Someone focused on studying amid their church duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the two middle pieces inside the church letters, and 'primarily' supplies the final letter from duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed means made thicker or more compact, concentrated as a liquid can be.

clue.text: Black ice, but not cold — dress for bed

parts.note: night is blackness

indicators.note: the cold letter is excluded from the frozen word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Warning of black ice, though not cold, so pyjamas will do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' strips the cold letter from the frozen word. 'Black ice' reads as one road hazard but is split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a loose dress worn to bed.

clue.text: Raise English tax in general

indicators.note: the tax is placed inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Lifting the English tax in broad terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' looks like 'broadly' but means inside LEE, the American Civil War general.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to lift up, to raise.

clue.text: Soldiers abandon cargo for battle

indicators.note: the soldiers walk out of the cargo word, leaving it

parts.note: freight is cargo
RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops leaving their freight behind to go to war.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a battle or combat.

clue.text: Fighters who inspire the soldiers

parts.note: to fire is to inspire, as with enthusiasm
men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Warriors who motivate the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighters' suggests combatants, but they are fire fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: Firemen are fire fighters.

clue.text: Wary of a drudge, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Being cautious of someone who does menial work.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarded means careful and cautious, wary.

clue.text: Resigns in order to make an entrance

indicators.note: the letters are put in order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone quits so as to make a grand entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order to' reads as 'so as to', but 'in order' rearranges RESIGNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act of going in, an entry.

clue.text: A student on board ship having a dance

indicators.note: the ship has the second a attached to it
the pair is aboard, set inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
taken as written
L is a learner, a student
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student aboard a ship joins in the dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts AL inside SS plus A, giving S-AL-SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Spoil access to south-east port

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a gate gives access

explanation.surface: Ruining the way into a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGATE is a seaside town and harbour in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a coastal town with a harbour in Kent, in the south-east of England.

clue.text: Before the dance, catch the game

indicators.note: the catching word comes before the dance word

parts.note: to net is to catch
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Grabbing a match before going off to the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport in which goals are scored through a high ring.

clue.text: Vagabond is crazy to accept toss of coin

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take the madness inside them
the coin's letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A drifter is foolish enough to stake things on a coin toss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toss of' makes NOIC, which 'to accept' wraps round the madness; 'Vagabond' is used as an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagabond life is a wandering one, without fixed home.

clue.text: Governing body ends year-long dispute

indicators.note: a dispute scrambles the words like an argument

explanation.surface: A ruling council finally settles a quarrel that lasted a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispute' rearranges ENDS YEAR-LONG. The General Synod is the governing assembly of the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The General Synod is the national assembly that governs the Church of England.
